sections.h2: How does probate work in New Mexico?
sections.html:
New Mexico runs probate under the Uniform Probate Code, Chapter 45 of the state statutes, and cases are filed with the county probate court where the person lived at death. The state court system includes 33 county probate courts alongside 34 district courts, according to the New Mexico Courts website.

The court guide for people without a lawyer says a probate can be filed anywhere from 5 days to 3 years after death, with a filing cost of $30. When there is a will, the court appoints the person named in it as personal representative, also called the executor. The document that gives that authority is called Letters Testamentary. With no will, the same authority comes in Letters of Administration.

For someone inheriting a house, the main question is who has authority to sign a deed. The answer depends on how the house was titled and whether a court has appointed anyone.

sections.h2: Which situations skip probate for a house?
sections.html:
Probate is not needed for real estate held in joint tenancy or with a recorded Transfer on Death Deed, according to the court guide. A surviving spouse can also transfer a community property home titled only in the deceased spouse's name by affidavit, filed six months after the death.

The small estate shortcut usually does not help with a house. A small estate is one worth less than $50,000 that does not include real property, and the successor can collect property using an Affidavit of Successor in Interest once 30 days have passed and no probate has been filed. Land, a house or a farm takes the estate outside that rule.

sections.h2: Who can act as personal representative?
sections.html:
New Mexico sets a priority order for appointment in Section 45-3-203. The person named in a probated will comes first, followed by the surviving spouse who is also a devisee, other devisees, the surviving spouse, other heirs, and, forty-five days after death, any creditor.

Someone with priority can nominate another qualified person by a signed writing filed with the court, and anyone of age can renounce. A person under the age of majority or found unsuitable in formal proceedings cannot serve. An objection to an appointment can be made only in formal proceedings.

This matters for a sale when several siblings share an inherited house. If they disagree about who serves, the court can step in, and nobody should sign a contract until the appointment is settled.

sections.h2: What does a personal representative do?
sections.html:
The personal representative gathers and inventories assets, notifies heirs, pays debts as far as estate funds allow, distributes the rest under the will or intestacy law and closes the case. The court guide says a case must stay open at least three months before it can be closed, by a sworn statement that the duties are complete.

The representative may not use estate funds for personal benefit but is entitled to fair compensation for time spent. Estate money can pay costs such as postage, filing fees and copies. The guide recommends keeping a written record of tasks and time.

  • Obtain Letters Testamentary or Letters of Administration before dealing with the house.
  • Locate the deed, mortgage statements and property tax bills.
  • Keep the property insured and the taxes current while the estate is open.
  • Keep a written log of work and expenses for the court and the heirs.

sections.h2: Who owns the house while probate is open?
sections.html:
Under Section 45-3-101, a person's separate property and share of community property devolves at death to the people named in the will, or to heirs if there is no will. Appellate decisions noted under the statute say real estate passes directly to heirs or devisees and not to the executor.

That ownership is still subject to administration, creditor rights and allowances. The surviving spouse's half of community property stays open to administration until the time to present claims has run, and after that only to the extent needed to pay community claims.

If the estate includes real property, the court guide says the representative may need to execute a Personal Representative's deed to move the property out of the decedent's name. The guide warns that deeds are tricky to draft and suggests hiring an attorney for that step.

sections.h2: How do creditor claims affect a sale?
sections.html:
A personal representative may publish a notice to creditors once a week for three successive weeks in a newspaper of general circulation in the county. Creditors then have four months from the first publication to present claims or be barred, under Section 45-3-801.

Known creditors can also receive written notice by mail or other delivery, and their deadline is the later of four months after publication or sixty days after the notice is delivered. The statute says the representative is not liable to anyone for giving or failing to give this notice, but a 1977 decision cited in the annotations held that publication of the hearing on a final account was not enough notice for known tort claimants.

For heirs planning to sell, this gives a rough timeline, since the claims window runs at least four months from the first publication.

sections.h2: Can a personal representative sell the house?
sections.html:
Yes, unless the will or a court order restricts it. Section 45-3-715 authorizes a representative acting reasonably for the benefit of interested persons to dispose of an asset, including land in New Mexico, for cash or on credit, at public or private sale.

The same section lets the representative make ordinary or extraordinary repairs, insure the assets, pay taxes and assessments and enter leases that extend past the period of administration. If part of the price is on credit, security is required for the unpaid balance unless the district court waives it for good cause.

  • A cash sale avoids the credit and security question altogether.
  • A sale as is can save the estate the cost of repairs, which the statute allows but does not require.
  • The estate can pay property taxes and insurance while the house is on the market.
  • If heirs disagree, a formal proceeding gives the court a role in resolving it.

Cash Home Buyers buys inherited houses in New Mexico as they are. We are not attorneys, and the personal representative should confirm authority with the estate's lawyer before accepting any offer.

sections.h2: What are the time limits and tax issues?
sections.html:
Most informal or formal probate proceedings cannot start more than three years after death, though Section 45-3-108 lists exceptions. One allows a later appointment if no proceedings have happened in the three years, but the representative then has limited rights to possess estate assets and claims other than administration expenses cannot be presented.

Property tax keeps running during probate. Taxes on real property are a lien from January 1 of the tax year, first in priority, under Section 7-38-48. Installments are due November 10 and April 10, and unpaid tax draws interest of one percent a month starting thirty days after the due date.

The assessed value of a house is capped at three percent annual growth, but a change of ownership resets it. The definition of change of ownership in Section 7-36-21.2 excludes some transfers, including a transfer to a child who lives in the home as a principal residence. A sale to an outside buyer is a change of ownership, so the buyer's bill can differ from the one the estate paid.

faqs.q: Do I need probate to sell an inherited house in New Mexico?
faqs.a: Usually yes if the house was in the decedent's sole name. Probate is not needed when the home was held in joint tenancy or had a recorded Transfer on Death Deed, and a surviving spouse can use an affidavit for a community property home six months after death.

faqs.q: What is the New Mexico small estate limit?
faqs.a: A small estate is worth less than $50,000 and has no real property. A house takes the estate outside the small estate procedure, so an Affidavit of Successor in Interest will not transfer it.

faqs.q: How long does probate take in New Mexico?
faqs.a: A case must stay open at least three months before it can be closed. Creditors have four months from first publication of the notice to present claims, so many estates run longer than three months.

faqs.q: How much does it cost to open probate in New Mexico?
faqs.a: The court guide lists a filing cost of $30. Attorney fees, publication costs and the personal representative's compensation are separate expenses the estate may pay.

faqs.q: What is the deadline to open a New Mexico probate?
faqs.a: A probate can be filed between 5 days and 3 years after death. After three years, only limited proceedings are allowed under Section 45-3-108.
